questions.answer: An AI workflow runs a model and tools through a fixed path that a developer defines, while an AI agent lets the model decide its own next steps and tools until the task is done [1][2]. Workflows are more predictable and easier to test, so they suit repeatable tasks, while agents suit open-ended work where the steps can't be known in advance [2]. Agents usually make more model calls and run slower, so Joe uses workflows by default and builds agents only when a task needs that flexibility [3]. For help deciding which one a project needs, see [AI agent vs AI workflow](/blog/ai-agent-vs-ai-workflow/) or the [contact page](/contact/).
